items.project_definition: The set of composite uniqueness requirements and logical limitations applied to data persistence to ensure integrity.
The implied security mechanism for storing sensitive credentials to meet the mentioned complexity requirements.
A temporal data type used for scheduling events and tracking system audit stamps.
A specific example of a short-form identifier assigned to a sports club.
The logical checks ensuring teams are distinct, dates are future-dated for upcoming states, and scores are present upon completion.
The associative links between entities, such as the foreign key dependencies between competitions, teams, and schedules.
The requirement that club names must remain globally distinct within the database.
The standardized time reference used to eliminate offset ambiguity for global event scheduling.
A 128-bit universally unique identifier used as the primary key for all main entities.
The verification process ensuring electronic mail addresses are unique and credentials meet minimum character lengths.
A join entity linking a person to a specific sporting event they wish to monitor.
The logic preventing a single person from creating multiple subscriptions to the same sporting event.
